key_insight: DemoPSD shows that self-distillation works better when teacher guidance is adjusted by disagreement, instead of using dense token-level supervision everywhere. This helps reduce overfitting to in-domain patterns and improves exploration and generalization.
problem_solved: The paper addresses a key weakness of on-policy self-distillation for LLM reasoning: privileged teacher supervision can become too rigid, suppress exploration, and hurt cross-domain performance.
method: Modulate self-distillation signals using disagreement between teacher and student predictions.
Reduce overconfident token-level supervision when the model is likely overfitting or relying too heavily on privileged information.
Preserve beneficial guidance while encouraging broader exploration and more robust reasoning behavior.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a more stable way to train reasoning models that generalize better beyond the training domain. It can improve distillation-based LLM training without sacrificing the benefits of teacher guidance.
visual_elements: Teacher-student pipeline diagram with privileged vs. student-only information
Disagreement heatmap over tokens showing where supervision is weakened or strengthened
